statement: (SGD regime only) With SGD-Nesterov, A1a (airbench96-style, 8.5 full-res epochs) reaches >=75.3% with a thin margin (0.7549, 7.22 s). It sits at a local optimum of zero-cost hyperparameters: augmentation, LS and the LR floor gave no gain >=0.3 pp (E008, E009, E015). Width changes trade badly (E005, E017). The local slope is steep, ~1 pp/epoch. Accuracy slack therefore had to come from a better optimizer or from cheaper epochs, not from retuning SGD. This happened (Muon E019, resolution E006/E021). The 'no retuning' lesson does NOT carry over to Muon (E027: one Muon hyperparameter moved accuracy by 1.18 pp).

Reproducing the futurebiohackers submission's defaults on this machine (fp16 + channels_last, compile max-autotune warmed up in build on synthetic data, GPU-resident uint8 data, GPU-side augmentation) gives a feasible starting point: 3-seed accuracy 0.7549 at 7.22 s.
The futurebiohackers defaults (8.5 epochs, bs 1024, last block 576) give a 3-seed mean accuracy >=0.753 and time <=9.0 s on the A100-SXM4, with complete == True.
Dirac (identity) init of the 3-conv group convs, which the reference recipe apparently lacks, speeds up early optimization. The airbench paper reports it saves about 1.2 epochs on CIFAR-10.
Adding dirac init and cutting epochs from 8.5 to 7.5 keeps 3-seed accuracy >=0.753 and reduces time by >=8% compared with the A1a reproduction.
Capacity in the last group (7x7/3x3 spatial) is cheap in FLOPs. Widening it lets the epoch count fall by more than the added per-epoch cost.
Last block at 768 with 7.5 epochs gives accuracy >=0.753 and time at least 3% below the 8.5-epoch / 576 reproduction.
Brightness/contrast augmentation, a hiverge CIFAR-10 trick, regularizes CIFAR-100 well enough to allow fewer epochs at equal accuracy.

Adding per-batch brightness (+/-0.07 to 0.14) and contrast (+/-0.065 to 0.13) jitter on the GPU at 8.0 epochs keeps 3-seed accuracy >=0.753, while the same 8.0-epoch recipe without it (the run measuring the epoch slope) falls below 0.753.

Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. Cost is FLOP-proportional for group-3 width (E117), depth (E123/E127/E130) and the late freeze. It is not FLOP-proportional for narrow group-2 widths (E080) or for pool and activation ops (E052, E023). FreezeOut's measured speedup exceeded its FLOP estimate by 1.3x (search), weak support for a byte term. Tip: E116/E119 code, ~4.26 s, population mean 0.7521. Yardstick (E128): pure cut ~0.054 pp per 1%, re-spend ~0.044 pp per 1%. Measured lever rates in pp per 1%: 85% freeze ~0.02 (banked); 85->80% ~0.06; 2/3/3 ~0.04; 3/3/2 ~0.08; group-2 freeze ~0.055; 16 px trim ~0.055-0.075; early bs 2048 ~0.2; late bs 1536 ~0.085. Live levers (untested): BN-eval in the frozen window (H2.20.6), group-3 width 512 (H2.19.2), a structural redesign of the 31x31 stage (earlier downsample or group-1 width; frontier node), lookahead removal (H9.2.2), activation under Muon (re-screen node), Muon-C (low). Closed: CUDA graphs, Inductor tuning, cuDNN settings, prepare, group-2 width, depth cuts, batch-size levers in every phase, freeze earlier than 85%, the 28 px substitution, phase trims, the group-2 freeze, the freeze anneal.

Progressive resizing makes early epochs much cheaper at little final-accuracy cost, provided the cheap phase uses efficient resolutions (24 px, or 16 px for the first ~2 epochs) rather than 26-28 px. The low-res operator (E016) and final-map geometry (E014) are second-order. Operator: flip + translate-2 at 32 px, then antialiased bilinear downsample, AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1); every shape is compiled and warmed up in build.
A 24->28->32 px schedule, with at most +0.5 epochs to compensate, cuts time by >=5% compared with the best fixed-32 px recipe while keeping accuracy >=0.753.
GELU is more expensive than SiLU or ReLU under compile/fp16, and swapping it costs no accuracy.
Replacing GELU with SiLU at equal epochs reduces time by >=2% and changes 3-seed accuracy by no more than 0.2 pp.

Training only on high-loss examples, as in Selective Backprop / airbench96_faster, cuts backward compute. With 500 images per class and ~8 epochs, the cost of the proxy or forward pass may outweigh the gain.
After 2 full epochs, backpropagating only the top 60% by loss of each batch (losses taken from the main net's own forward pass) reduces time by >=5% with accuracy >=0.753.

(SGD full-res regime) Fixed and per-step CPU/launch overhead (timed prepare, Python/kernel-launch overhead, separate optimizer kernels) is a measurable share of the ~7 s SGD run, and removing it cuts time without touching accuracy.
Compiling the whole train step (forward, backward and a fused optimizer) or capturing it in CUDA graphs removes launch overhead at bs 1024.
A fused/foreach optimizer plus a CUDA-graphed or fully compiled step reduces time by >=2% compared with the reproduction, with accuracy within 0.2 pp.
Prepare (uint8 upload, normalization, whitening init on 5000 images) takes a non-trivial share of timed time and can be shrunk, e.g. fewer whitening images or fused normalization on the GPU.
In the reproduction, prepare is >=3% of prepare+train time. Computing the whitening statistics on 1000-2000 images instead of 5000 cuts prepare by >=30% with accuracy within 0.2 pp.
A larger batch (2000) halves the step count and per-step overhead and raises GPU utilization. LR, wd and momentum need retuning to keep accuracy.
bs 2000 with LR scaled by the kilostep rule, at equal epochs, reduces time by >=3% while keeping accuracy >=0.753.

Accuracy noise sets the usable margin, and decisions near the gate select for luck. Single-component model (E113, one calibration pair): fp-level differences fully decorrelate a seed's trajectory. Per-trajectory sd ~0.26 pp, with no persistent seed component (paired sd 0.36 = sqrt(2) x 0.26). Expected sds: 3-seed scored mean ~0.15 pp; 100-seed mean ~0.026 pp; two-arm SE = 0.26*sqrt(1/nA+1/nB). Consequences: (1) 8-22-seed deltas of ~0.1 pp are noise (E104 vs E121). (2) Gate passes are population margin plus luck. The banked E116 code (population 0.7521) passes with p ≈ Phi((0.7521-0.753)/0.15) ≈ 27%. Its scored rows E116/E118/E119/E121/E122/E123*/E128 are 0.7501/0.7520/0.7531/0.7516/0.7505/0.7516/0.7533: 2 of 7 pass, mean 0.7517, consistent with the model. *E123's provenance is unresolved: its idea says it reran E090, but its time matches E116 (H4.2.4). (3) The official 40-seed mean has sd ~0.04 pp, so a population mean >= ~0.7513 clears 0.75 almost surely. (4) Margin is gone, so further accuracy-costing cuts must be funded. Open hint: E100's 5 distinct scored rows average 0.7543 vs its 0.7530 population (~2 SE), a possible recipe x seeds 0-2 offset (H4.9.1).

For the compiled SGD recipe (A1a), per-seed accuracy is bit-deterministic and run-to-run time variation is small (CV <=0.5%) once compile is warmed up in build. This does NOT hold for the compiled-Muon + progressive-resize tip (E028: per-seed differences of -0.27/+0.19/-0.59 pp on an identical rerun).
Rerunning the identical A1a config gives bit-identical per-seed accuracy and a mean time within 2% of the first run.
Swapping the optimizer (Muon on the conv filters, SGD for biases and head) does not reduce time-to-75% on CIFAR-100, despite its CIFAR-10 gains.
On CIFAR-100, Muon's orthogonalized updates give no sample-efficiency gain over well-tuned high-LR SGD-Nesterov at the airbench96 widths, and the Newton-Schulz steps add per-step cost.
Muon (lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, 3 NS steps) on the conv filters, at the same epochs as the reproduction, gives accuracy no higher than SGD +0.2 pp and time no lower than SGD -2%.

The full-res accuracy-vs-epochs curve near A1a is steep below 8.5 epochs (E007: -0.48 pp for -0.5 ep, ~0.95 pp/epoch, plausibly 0.4-1.5 pp given ~0.25 pp SE) and flatter above 8.5 (reference ablation: 9 ep 75.6% vs 8.5 ep 75.5%). A full-res epoch costs ~0.85 s (~11.8% of time), so cutting full-res epochs costs ~0.08 pp per 1% of time. Every time-saving trade-off must beat this rate.
Unmodified A1a at 8.0 epochs (LR/EMA schedules rescaled to the step count) gives time 6.75-6.85 s and 3-seed accuracy 0.749-0.754, i.e. a loss of <=0.6 pp per 0.5 epoch removed.

Phase-dependent bottleneck. 32 px (cap 94-100% of the time) and 24 px (cap 84%) are energy-bound, so time tracks fwd/bwd energy and memory traffic. 16 px is not at the cap (282 W) but is 98% GPU-busy (E052), so it is bound by low-occupancy kernels and per-step GPU work. Per-step optimizer work costs time at every resolution. It shows up as idle-free GPU work at 16 px (~2 ms per removed step, E038) and as energy at 32 px (E084: +~65 steps at 32 px cost +0.11 s, ~1.7 ms/step). Per-step savings in the 32 px phase (lookahead, renorm, Muon momentum traffic) are therefore live levers. FLOP and byte levers transfer best to the 300 W PCIe judge.

NVML sampling at >=10 Hz during an untimed run of the E026 tip shows board power >=95% of the 400 W cap for >=80% of the 32 px phase. During the 16 px and 24 px phases power stays below 90% of the cap for >=30% of the time, i.e. those phases are launch- or per-step-bound. Observational only; no sleeps or idle gaps added.

Most of E006's -0.69 pp came from the degenerate 2x2 final map at 24 px (24->23->11->5->2, vs 3x3 at 26-32 px); raising the low-res stage to >=26 px recovers most of the loss. (The original random-resized-crop half is retired as moot: E006 never used random-resized crop.)

E006's 9.0-epoch schedule with 26 px instead of 24 px for the first phase, flip + translate-2 at 32 px followed by antialiased downsample (no random-resized crop), gives 3-seed accuracy >=0.752 (>= +0.4 pp over E006) at time <=6.3 s.

With the same 26->28->32 schedule, crop mode (random 26/28 px crops of the flipped/translated 32 px image, no rescaling) gives >=0.3 pp higher 3-seed accuracy than antialiased-resize mode at equal time (+/-1%).

A 9.0-epoch schedule with 26 px for 0-30%, 28 px for 30-60% and 32 px for the last 40% (EfficientTrain++-style long full-res tail), with flip + translate and antialiased downsample, gives 3-seed accuracy >=0.755 and time <=6.7 s (>=7% below A1a's 7.22 s).

In the tip code (E026 lineage), the flip/translate/resize augmentation RNG comes from the trial seed and is reset in prepare. A logged hash of the first batch's augmentation parameters differs across seeds 0-2, and repeating seed 0 reproduces it. E006's 0.02 pp per-seed spread was chance.

Conv FLOPs at 32 px are concentrated in group 2 (~48%: conv1 at 15x15 128->384 plus conv2/3 at 7x7 384->384), then group 3 (~32%) and group 1 (~20%) (estimate from the reference's shapes). Narrowing group 2 is the largest width lever (384->320 cuts ~15% of FLOPs); narrowing group 1 (128->96) saves only ~7%. The reference ablations show capacity is costly to remove on CIFAR-100, so the cut must be paired with the extra epochs it buys.
At 8.5 full-res epochs, group 2 width 384->320 cuts time by >=8% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.4 pp versus A1a, i.e. a better exchange rate than cutting epochs (0.08 pp per 1%).

Zero-time-cost accuracy levers on the current architecture and schedule. Scalar knobs are exhausted: Muon floor, warmup in both directions, head lr 0.4x, head wd, MaxSup, LS 0.2, the bias freeze earlier (E093) and at 20% (E061), lookahead removal (E092), and EMA window/LAWA with BN buffers copied from the net (E081, E083). The one remaining candidate with external support is end-of-run averaging that keeps the BN buffers consistent with the averaged weights (H6.5.4; search 2411.18704: BN, not the parameters, breaks long-window EMA). Phase-local Muon lr is under H10, and filter Muon lr under H7. Retire H6 if H6.5.4 fails.
Budgeted-training results favor LR decaying to zero at the end of a fixed budget. The reference decays only to 0.07x, which leaves end-of-budget gradient noise that hurts final accuracy.
A1a with the LR decaying to 0 at the last step instead of 0.07x (warmup unchanged) raises 3-seed accuracy by >=0.2 pp, with time within +/-1%.

After progressive resizing, BN statistics and the EMA weights are dominated by low-res epochs. Re-estimating BN statistics at 32 px on training data at the end of train (FixRes-style) removes the train/test resolution mismatch cheaply.

On a 24->32 progressive schedule, a forward-only BN re-estimation pass at 32 px over ~10% of an epoch of augmented training data, run inside train, raises 3-seed accuracy by >=0.2 pp at <2% time cost.

Run-to-run noise on the 3-seed scored mean (~0.15 pp sd, from 0.26/sqrt(3)) is the decision-relevant noise for the gate, and picking whichever near-threshold variant first clears 0.753 selects for luck (E026, E046, E068, E090, E096, E100). Comparisons must count distinct trajectories, not runs: two bit-identical scored runs are one sample.

Three neutral perturbations of A1a (a different 5000-image whitening subset, an alternative equivalent autotune choice, an fp16 vs fp32 normalization path) give 3-seed means with std between 0.1 and 0.3 pp.

A1a's mean accuracy over extra seeds 3-10, run through the benchmark's own trial code without editing benchmark/, is >=0.751. That is about 0.4 pp below its seeds 0-2 mean at most, so the baseline is feasible but not comfortably above the 0.75 official bar.

Accuracy at a fixed short budget tracks total training epochs/steps far more than the share spent at 32 px: a 24 px epoch carries most of a 32 px epoch's accuracy value at 57% of its cost. Evidence pattern: E013 put 1.8x more epochs at 32 px than E006 yet gained only +0.26 pp, and E006 (9 ep, mostly low-res) is only 0.22 pp behind 8 full-res epochs (E007) while costing 0.92 s less.
With the E006 operator and no 28 px phase, 6@24 + 4@32 px (10 epochs, ~6.5 s by the cost table) gives >=0.3 pp higher 3-seed accuracy than 4@24 + 5@32 px (9 epochs, ~6.4 s), with time within +2%.

A two-stage 24->32 px schedule (E006 operator, no 28 px phase) at 9.5-10 total epochs, with 24 px for <=60% of steps and LR/EMA rescaled to the step count, gives 3-seed accuracy >=0.753 at time <=6.6 s (>=8.6% below A1a). Predicted time = per-epoch cost table (24 px 0.485 s, 32 px 0.848 s) + ~0.2 s overhead.

16 px epochs are cheap (0.30x of a 32 px epoch at bs 1536, E045). Each early 24->16 swap costs roughly 0.2-0.35 pp, but these are single-run point estimates against references that were often lucky draws (±0.15 pp). The third swap (E046) cost more than the head-on-Muon gain bought: the tip family pools to 0.7533. No further whole-epoch swap is affordable. Giving part of the 24 px bridge back while cutting total epochs (E047) may beat the 3@16 swap at equal time.

A compiled per-epoch cost measurement (2 epochs each, no scored run) shows a 20 px epoch <=0.45x and a 16 px epoch <=0.35x the cost of a 32 px epoch. A 16->24->32 schedule (e.g. 2@16 + 4@24 + 4@32) then reaches >=0.753 at <=6.3 s.

On this energy-bound GPU the optimizer step count is nearly free in time (E010: half the steps, same time), and more updates help accuracy at a fixed epoch budget (E010: bs 2000 cost -0.81 pp). Smaller batches (512-768) should therefore buy accuracy at roughly equal time, unless smaller GEMMs lose efficiency (E012).
A1a at bs 768 (LR/wd/EMA scaled by the same kilostep rule as E010, in reverse), 8.5 epochs, gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.757 with time within +3% of 7.22 s.

GELU's exact erf costs measurable energy in the fused BN+activation kernels (E003: SiLU saved 2.2%). A cheaper GELU approximation (tanh or polynomial) keeps GELU's accuracy advantage while saving part of that cost, and stacks on any schedule.
Replacing exact GELU with GELU(approximate='tanh') on A1a reduces time by >=1% with a 3-seed accuracy within 0.25 pp of A1a (>=0.7525).

Full-res A1a at 9.0 epochs (LR/EMA rescaled to the step count) gains <=0.3 pp over 8.5 epochs (3-seed accuracy <=0.758) at 7.6-7.7 s, i.e. the slope above 8.5 epochs is less than half the measured 8.0->8.5 slope.

Optimizer quality per update was the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~7-8 epochs, and Muon was the lever: +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter epoch slope (E020), large-batch tolerance (E022, E038). Closed: momentum (on 3-seed evidence; re-screen node), NS count, cheaper orthogonalizers, Muon lr in every phase (E105, E107, E110, E111), freeze LR anneal (E129), NorMuon (retired on the row-norm argument). The head on Muon and head lr 0.5x are kept, but a population-level audit is pending (H13.1.1). Muon-C is very low prior: its gains are long-budget, overhead ~2x, and E033 shows conditioning does not bind. Schedule shape (H7.4) is very low prior.

Muon momentum and lr sit near a local optimum. Momentum is flat in 0.5-0.6 and steep above (E027 -1.18 pp at 0.85). For lr, effects >=~0.15 pp are excluded from 0.20 to ~0.36 effective across all phases (E034, E105, E107, E110, E111, each within +/-0.09 pp on 8-66 trajectories). That does not show the lr is flat to +/-0.05. Muon lr scaling is closed as a lever at the current instrument's resolution.

On the E026 tip, Muon momentum 0.5 (lr 0.24, Nesterov, everything else unchanged) gives a 3-seed accuracy no higher than 0.7574 (tip estimate 0.7554 + 0.2 pp) at equal time. Lowering momentum does not buy usable slack.
On the E026 tip, Muon lr 0.20 (momentum 0.6) gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7575 (>= +0.2 pp over the 0.7554 estimate) at equal time (+/-1%).

Muon's remaining overhead is a fixed per-step cost (NS matmuls plus stacking/momentum kernels), ~1.7-2 ms per step at every resolution: idle-free small kernels at 16 px (E038) and energy at 32 px (E084). Renorm cadence saved ~0.08 ms/step (E035). NS 3->2 cost 1.8 pp (E031) and NS 4 bought nothing (E033). External work finds orthogonalizer variants accuracy-equivalent (search: randomized/inexact polar ~= full), so only step count or cheaper per-step traffic can save time. Cheaper orthogonalizers are closed.

On the E026 tip, renormalizing Muon weights every 2 + int(15*progress) steps instead of every step (inside the compiled update, with the step flag passed as a tensor so nothing recompiles) cuts time by >=1.5% with a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7535.

On the E026 tip, 2 Newton-Schulz steps with per-iteration Polar-Express-style coefficients (instead of 3 fixed-coefficient steps) cut time by >=2% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.2 pp against the 0.7554 estimate.

On the compiled-Muon E026 tip, bs 1536 (SGD groups scaled by the kilostep rule, Muon lr/momentum unchanged, LR/EMA/lookahead rescaled to the step count) cuts time by >=3% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.25 pp against the 0.7554 estimate.

The local yardstick, measured on the tip (E128, 100 seeds per arm): 32 px phase -0.25 / +0.25 epoch gave -0.25 / +0.24 pp, i.e. ~1 pp per 32 px epoch. As rates: pure cut ~0.054 pp per 1% of time, re-spend ~0.044 pp per 1%. A low-res trim has now been measured at large seed: 16 px 2->1.5 epochs cost -0.17 pp for -3.1% (E132), no better than the 32 px rate. Equal-time low-res/high-res reshuffles are null (E114). Every phase trim now trades at or above the yardstick.

A 4@16 + 4.5@32 px schedule (8.5 total epochs, step-indexed switch, LR/EMA/lookahead rescaled to the step count, E026 operator and compiled Muon) gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.755 at time <=5.45 s (estimate: 4x0.27 + 4.5x0.85 + Muon/fixed overhead).

An untimed compiled cost measurement (2 epochs each) shows a 12 px epoch >=0.22x and a 20 px epoch 0.40-0.50x the cost of a 32 px epoch. The floor comes from Muon's fixed per-step cost and from small-kernel inefficiency, so replacing a 16 px epoch with 12 px saves <1.5% of total time and is not worth pursuing.

The tip's run-to-run nondeterminism comes from per-process cuDNN algorithm picks (cudnn.benchmark), not from Muon max-autotune. E036 (deterministic cuDNN plus default-mode Muon) gave a bit-identical seed-0 rerun. E042 (default-mode Muon only) stayed nondeterministic (0.7522/0.7549/0.7530). Pinning cuDNN costs ~9.8% time (E036), so determinism is not usable in scored runs. It is a measurement convenience, not a score lever. AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1)'s atomic backward is an unlikely co-source: with a 1x1 output, each gradient goes to a single argmax and nothing collides.

With the Muon update compiled without max-autotune (mode='default') and cuDNN algorithm selection pinned (cudnn.benchmark=False or deterministic algorithms for the 16/24/32 px shapes), two identical runs of the tip give bit-identical per-seed accuracies, with time within +1.5% of 5.50 s.
LS 0.3 was found optimal under SGD (E009, futurebiohackers sweep). Muon fits faster and tuned public Muon recipes use LS 0.09, so the tip may be over-regularized.
On the E026 tip, label smoothing 0.2 instead of 0.3 gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7575 (>= +0.2 pp over the 0.7554 estimate) at equal time.

Per-phase batch size, read through critical batch size. Early (16/24 px): B_crit lies between 1536 and 2048. Going smaller gains nothing (E121, bs 1024: +0.004 pp at 100 seeds); going larger costs a lot (E134, bs 2048 with step-fixed warmup: -0.30 pp; confounded by fewer whitening-bias steps and the SGD rescale). Late (28/32 px): bs 1024 is a real purchase. E126 at 100 seeds shows bs 1536 costs -0.18 pp for -2.1%, ~0.085 pp per 1%, which confirms the direction of E084 (the E121 note calling E084 'likely noise' was wrong about direction). Open puzzle: the late B_crit looks smaller than the early one, the reverse of gradient-noise-scale theory (1812.06162). E126's confounds (EMA-window samples, SGD rescale, Muon path length) may produce this; H11.2.2 decides. Batch size is closed as a time lever in both phases.

On the tip lineage, use bs 2048 for the 2@16 + 2@24 epochs and bs 1024 for the 4@32 epochs. LR warmup/decay, EMA, lookahead and renorm are indexed by samples seen, and the SGD groups are scaled per phase by the kilostep rule (Muon lr/momentum unchanged). All batch/resolution shapes are compiled and warmed up in build. Prediction: time <=5.26 s (within +1% of E038) and 3-seed accuracy >=0.755. If time is >=5.35 s, the per-step-bound explanation of E038 is wrong.

On the E046 tip (bs 1536), raise only the 16/24 px phases to bs 3072, except the first 0.5 epoch, which stays at bs 1536. The 32 px tail stays at bs 1536. Keep the LR warmup fixed in steps (not samples), so the E043 warmup confound is removed. Decay, EMA and lookahead are indexed by samples. Prediction: time <=4.85 s (>=2% below E046) with a two-run accuracy >=0.7535. Low priority: run only after H8.1.1 indicates whether early batch size, not warmup steps, drove E043's loss.

Only the 16 px phase is launch- or per-step-bound (E045: 282 W, util 82%, ~0.8 s of the tip's time). Capturing the whole train step (fwd, bwd, SGD foreach, compiled Muon, lookahead) in a CUDA graph for the 16 px shape alone removes idle gaps there. The ceiling is ~0.14 s (~3%), with a realistic gain of 1-2%. Graphing 24/32 px gains nothing because those phases sit at the power cap. Fable shows per-resolution whole-step graphs are feasible but publishes no isolated gain, and its 7.6% came mostly from resizing. The gain is per-step, so it transfers poorly to the 300 W PCIe judge.

On the E046 tip (after static shapes, N1a, if that is banked), CUDA-graph the full train step for the 16 px shape only. Capture and warm it up in build on synthetic data, with static input buffers, the LR as 0-d tensors, and a renorm on/off graph-key variant. Prediction: time drops by >=1% (<=4.905 s on E046, or 1% below the N1a tip) with a two-run accuracy >=0.7535. Gate: run only if H2.4.2 shows wall time >=1.3x GPU-busy time at 16 px.

Untimed CUDA-event and profiler timing of the E046 tip per phase. Per step, wall time exceeds GPU-busy time by >=30% at 16 px, and by <10% at both 24 px and 32 px (E045: 24 px is at the cap 84% of the time). Observational only. This gates H2.12.1 and N2c.

The LR warmup was rescaled from ~408 SGD steps to ~256 steps (bs 1536). Halving it (E051, 0.7528) is -0.05 pp against the pooled 0.7533, which is noise, so neither direction is established. The post-mortem mechanism ('warmup protects the 64x-LR SGD biases') has no supporting effect.

On the E038 tip, halving the LR warmup length (in steps; everything else unchanged) gives a 3-seed accuracy >=0.7562 (>= +0.2 pp over the 0.7542 two-run mean) at equal time. If both halving and doubling stay within +/-0.15 pp, warmup is closed.

End-of-run schedule under Muon. The tail (floor-hold at ~96% of steps, lookahead stop, final 8-step EMA at 0.3 lerp every 4, eval on EMA weights with BN buffers from the net) costs no time and is kept. Its mean gain was never shown, though: the evidence is E068 (one high draw) and E069, and no tail vs no-tail off-seed A/B was ever run. Longer windows lost off-seed (E081 -0.09, ~1 SE; E083 LAWA -0.29, ~2 SE). Two explanations compete: (a) averaging higher-LR pre-floor iterates hurts; (b) the averaged weights mismatch the BN buffers copied from the net. External work (2411.18704) directly supports (b). Only H6.5.4 separates them.

On the E056 base, change the Muon-group LR floor from 0.07x to 0.05x and nothing else. Prediction: a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7548 (+0.15 pp over the pooled 0.7533) at equal time (±0.5%). A result within ±0.15 pp closes it.

Muon flattened the epoch slope, so a group-2 width cut might trade like a schedule trim. E050 (384->352) saved only half its FLOP-proportional time. NVIDIA's tile-quantization guidance explains this: 352 rounds up to 3x128-wide N-tiles, the same work as 384, and 320 does too on 128-wide tiles. Only tile-aligned widths (256, or 320 if cuDNN picks 64-wide tiles) can save FLOP-proportional time. A cut to 256 is a large capacity loss (E017: 320 cost 0.94 pp under SGD), so the prior for a profitable width cut stays low. Decide with existing profile data and a per-layer profile, never with a scored run first.

On the E038 tip, narrow group 2 from 384 to 352 channels (recompiled and warmed up in build). Prediction: time drops >=3.5% with a 3-seed accuracy loss <=0.2 pp vs 0.7542, i.e. <=0.06 pp per 1%, beating bs 1536's 0.064.

Untimed side check: the E038 tip code run through the benchmark's trial code on seeds 3-10 has a mean >=0.7530 and lies within 0.15 pp of its seeds 0-2 two-run mean (0.7542). Then the official 40-seed mean clears 0.75 with >=0.25 pp to spare.

Unbundled determinism probe on the E038 tip: compile the Muon update with mode='default', keep cudnn.benchmark=True, and change nothing else. A real whitening-bias freeze is a FLOP/byte time lever. Detach the bias in forward (Fable e1 and hiverge: F.conv2d(x, w, b if grad else b.detach())), or set requires_grad=False (airbench: 'disable their gradient to increase backward-pass throughput ... without reducing accuracy'). The stem output then needs no grad, so autograd skips group-1 conv1's dgrad (~1.9% of conv FLOPs, low tensor-core efficiency), the stem GELU backward and the bias reduction. Estimated saving ~1-2.5%. As a FLOP lever it should transfer to the 300 W judge. The reference recipes train the bias for only 0.2 epoch (~7 steps at bs 1536, ~3% of steps), with its LR decaying to 0 over that window, then detach. E061 (LR=0 at 20% of steps, -0.08 pp, noise) covers accuracy only for the 20%-of-steps freeze point, and it saved no time.

On the verified tip, detach the whitening bias (hiverge pattern) from step 0.2*total onward, i.e. E061's freeze point, which falls inside the 16 px phase. Use two static compiled graphs keyed on whiten_bias_grad; only the 16 px shape needs both variants, and all are warmed up in build on synthetic data. Confirm in the compiled backward graph that group-1 conv1's dgrad and the stem backward are gone. Prediction: two scored runs average >=1.0% below the base's pooled time (outside the ±0.6% noise band), with accuracy within 0.1 pp of the base on the off-seed seeds 3-10 check. If the time drop is <0.4%, the dgrad is not skipped or is negligible, and H2.15 is refuted as a time lever. Move to an earlier freeze (~0.2 epoch) only after the saving is verified.

Fused BN/GELU/elementwise Triton kernels take 29-31% of GPU time at 24/32 px (E067), but the cost is spread over ~211 kernels per step; the top kernel takes ~0.43 ms/step. Inductor tuning flags are near-optimal and blow the build budget (E066). Torch 2.4 has no fused normalization-backward codegen (that arrived ~2.11), so BN backward likely reads dy and x in separate reduction and dX passes. The only lever left is a hand-written Triton fused BN(+GELU) backward for the dominant 32 px layers. It is math-equivalent and saves energy-proportional bytes, but it costs high effort and has a bounded gain. A bias-only BN (frozen weight), as in Fable/hiverge, saves essentially no backward compute, because dX needs both per-channel reductions anyway.

The Muon filters feed BN, so the effective relative update size is (Muon step)/||w||, and the renorm target norm acts as a second, implicit LR schedule. hiverge and Fable decay the renorm target linearly from 0.5012 to 0.0786 over the run. Combined with the LR decay to 0.05x, that keeps the relative step from collapsing late (it ends at ~0.3x instead of 0.05x of its start value). The tip adopted hiverge's renorm cadence (E035), but the tree has never examined its target-norm schedule. If the tip renorms to a constant norm, its late relative step is much smaller than in the CIFAR-10 SOTA recipes. This is a change of schedule shape across the whole run, not the end-only floor change that E057 found null.

First check in the tip code whether filter renorm uses a constant target (free, no run). Change nothing else. Prediction: an off-seed seeds 3-10 mean >= tip +0.15 pp and a two-run scored pool >= tip pool +0.1 pp, at time within ±0.6%. If the off-seed delta is within ±0.1 pp, the implicit schedule is not binding and N9a is refuted. If the tip already decays its target, retire N9a without a run.

If the off-seed loss is >=0.15 pp, lookahead is carrying real smoothing on the ~240-step schedule, and the line closes.

Calibrate the off-seed instrument before more off-seed verdicts. Run the unchanged tip on seeds 3-10 in fresh processes until there are >=2 non-bit-identical samples, which samples the training-divergence mode. Prediction: the sd of the 8-seed off-seed mean across non-identical reruns is 0.07-0.15 pp, so a paired A/B difference has SE ~0.1-0.2 pp, and each of E077/E078/E079/E081/E084's off-seed deltas is <1.5 SE. If the sd is <0.05 pp, the instrument is sharp and the past off-seed verdicts stand.

(Weakened) Late full-resolution training binds accuracy. What holds: fresh 32 px images matter (E124, ~-0.9 pp from duplicates), late updates matter on the downside (E126, -0.18 pp; confounded by EMA-window samples, SGD rescale and Muon path length), and 32 px epochs give ±1 pp per epoch (E128). What is NOT shown: that late training is special. Early decrements cost as much or more (E134 -0.30, E132 -0.17), and no late increment has been tested at large seed. Late Muon lr (E100/E110/E111) and an equal-time 24/32 swap (E114) are null. Distinguishing test: a late increment (H2.11.5) after the E126 confound ablation (H11.2.2). If late increments also saturate, H11 collapses into the frontier Lvl1.

Resolution-statistics adaptation. The antialiased downsample changes patch statistics, so each resolution switch shifts the stem-output distribution. The 64x-LR whitening bias and the BN affine parameters absorb that shift. Freezing the bias before the later switches removes this adaptation. Evidence: E093 (freezing at 0.2 epoch cost -0.44 pp off-seed and -0.5 pp scored, the largest clearly real recent effect). The current freeze sits at ~41% of samples, inside the 24 px phase, before the 28 and 32 px switches.

Move the whitening-bias freeze from ~41% to ~70% of samples. Prediction: >= +0.1 pp off-seed. Outcome E102: off-seed 0.00 vs tip, scored 0.7521, time +1.2%. The 70% point covers both later resolution switches, so the adaptation mechanism was tested and gave nothing. Closed; never-freeze not worth a run.

Placement of updates. Added steps at low resolution buy nothing (E121, +0.004 pp at 100 seeds), while late 28/32 px steps are worth ~0.18 pp for ~2.1% time (E126, at ~5 SE). Caveat: E126 changes three things besides step count: the last-8-step EMA/lookahead window covers 1.5x more samples (E081 showed longer windows hurt), the SGD groups are kilostep-rescaled, and Muon path length falls by 1/3. The confound ablation decides whether update count is the mechanism.

Same run as H10.1.1, opposite prediction: an off-seed gain <= +0.03 pp from ~53 added low-res steps; a gain >= +0.08 refutes it. Outcome E104: +0.12 off-seed (one process), scored -0.13 pp vs the tip pool. Leans toward refutation. Needs a large-seed paired replicate.

(Restated as a lever) A larger phase-local Muon lr buys >=0.1 pp at zero time. Tests: low-res x1.5 (E107) -0.02, 28 px x1.25 (E111) +0.03, 32 px x1.5 vs x1.25 (E110) -0.07, pooled E100 (32 px x1.25) vs E090 +0.01 (22-66 trajectories each, SE ~0.05-0.08). Effects >=~0.15 pp are excluded; the mechanistic contrast with update count is not established because the update-count gain itself is ~1 SE.

Raise the conv-filter Muon lr x1.25 in the 32 px phase only (E100). Prediction: off-seed >= +0.08 pp at equal time. Outcome: pooled off-seed E100 0.7527 (3 processes) vs E090 ~0.7525, i.e. +0.01-0.02. E110 (x1.5) gave -0.07 vs x1.25. No population effect. E100's scored advantage (distinct 0.7561/0.7516/0.7551, mean 0.7543, vs E090 0.7515) is confined to seeds 0-2.

(Gated) A late increment: bs 768 in the last ~1 epoch of the 32 px phase. Run only after H11.2.2 shows that E126's loss came from update count. Step 1, untimed: profile bs 768 at 32 px (static, warmed) and project total time. Step 2: 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline (sample-indexed; final-EMA/lookahead pinned to the last 8 steps; SGD groups kilostep-scaled; Muon unchanged). Prediction (H11): gain >=+0.08 pp at <=+2.5% time, i.e. >=0.05 pp per 1%, beating the 0.044 re-spend rate. Prediction (frontier Lvl1): gain <=0.044 pp per 1%. If the gain is <=0.03 pp, increments saturate late too.

In build, set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark_limit=0 so cuDNN v8 tries every available conv algorithm for each static train shape (16/24/28/32 px, bs 1536/1024) and the eval path, instead of the default 10. Change nothing else, and check that build stays under 600 s. Log per-phase epoch times and per-(layer, shape) conv kernel names against the E090 defaults, which also feeds H4.5.1. Prediction: at least one 24/28/32 px shape picks a different kernel, and mean total time falls by >=0.8% over two scored runs. Accuracy is math-equivalent within noise (distinct pool within 0.1 pp of the E090 family). If the kernel names are identical to the default picks, or time changes by <0.3%, the lever is closed.

Depth cuts are FLOP-proportional time levers but do not beat the yardstick. 2/3/3: -0.29 pp for -7.0% (~0.04 pp per 1%, E127). Re-spent at 32 px at the upward rate (~0.044 pp per 1%, E128 +0.25 arm), it roughly breaks even, and additivity is untested. 3/3/2: -0.48 pp for -6.3% (~0.08 pp per 1%, E130). Closed.

Untimed first. On the E100 net, profile per-step time and NVML energy at 32/28 px (bs 1024) and 24 px (bs 1536) for three variants, each reducing one group's residual branch to a single conv plus the skip: (a) group 2, (b) group 1, (c) group 3. Prediction: at least one variant cuts projected total run time by >=6%. Score only that variant, with the 32 px phase lengthened to spend half the saving (net ~-3%), and decide on the large-seed paired instrument (H4.6.1), requiring a loss <=0.05 pp vs E100. Expect a capacity loss similar to E017. If no variant saves >=6%, close depth cuts without a scored run.

The judge is a 300 W A100 PCIe; local runs are on a 400 W SXM4. Untimed analysis of existing NVML logs (E045, E116 step-1 profile, E100), with no power-limit changes: project each candidate's judge time as the sum over phases of max(phase energy / 300 W, phase GPU-busy time). Prediction: E116's freeze saving is a larger fraction on the projected judge than locally (>=1.1x), because it removes energy-bound backward bytes, while bs-1024 per-step levers transfer worse. Use only to break ties between configs whose local times are within 3%.

Extended off-seed instrument and tip decision (E090 vs E095 on seeds 3-26). Outcome: E098 confirmed E090 at 0.7525 but ran E096 instead of E095, one process per arm. Superseded by H4.2.8 and the large-seed instrument H4.6.1.

Re-decide the tip lineage with the corrected instrument. Free step first: compute the within-seed cross-process sd from the existing E028/E094/E098/E106 per-seed logs and checksums. Status: (2) met, pooled E100 - E090 ~ +0.02 pp, so E100's x1.25 is not a population gain. (1) partly contradicted, E106 implies ~0.14 pp per-seed cross-process sd, not >=0.2. (3) untested, E095 (bs 1024 at 32 px on the 4@32 schedule) - E090 >= +0.08 pp, to be decided on the large-seed instrument (H4.6.1).

The 24 px bridge buys accuracy at a better rate than the 32 px phase. Old evidence: E064/E065 vs E062/E063 (+0.12 pp for +0.9%) and E070's trim (-0.25 pp for -1.8%, against a lucky pool). New: E108 (2@16 + 1.75@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.5@32 vs E100) gave +0.09 off-seed over 3 processes (22 seeds) at +0.3% time. Scored was 0.7527 in two bit-identical runs, i.e. one distinct sample, which is weaker evidence than the 3-process off-seed. Leans toward support but is within ~1 SE (H4.6).

On E100 code, run 2@16 + 1.75@24 (bs 1536) + 1.25@28 + 2.5@32 (bs 1024): +0.5 epoch at 24 px funded by -0.25 epoch at 32 px. Prediction: pooled off-seed gain >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes, and distinct scored samples not below E100's. Outcome E108/E109: off-seed +0.09 (3 processes, 22 seeds), scored 0.7527 in one distinct sample (two bit-identical runs), time +0.3%. Leans toward support but stays inconclusive. Decide with H8.2.2.

Under Muon, data composition and augmentation strength are zero-time accuracy sources, and the current setting may sit above the short-budget optimum. Evidence: the accuracy response to augmentation and coverage is steep. Translate 4 cost ~-0.6 pp (E131) and halving unique 32 px coverage ~-0.9 pp (E124), both at 100 seeds. Class balance is null (E112). Augmentation was closed after testing only the upward direction. The recipe is under-trained (~1 pp per 32 px epoch, E128), which favors weaker augmentation, especially in the late 28/32 px phases. Live: translate 1/0 and flip removal late (weaker augmentation node).

Multi-sample augmentation at equal compute: 2+ augmented copies of the same image within a minibatch at fixed batch size and step count. Fort et al. (2105.13343) find +1.6 pp on CIFAR-100 at multiplicity 4, but only at ~8,000 sample-epochs, where coverage is not a constraint. At ~7.5 epochs, halving unique-image coverage is a real risk, and alternating flip already lowers augmentation variance. Low prior.

On E100, in the 32 px phase only (bs 1024), build each batch from 768 unique images plus 256 repeated images with an independent augmentation draw (opposite flip, independent translate). Samples per step, step count and shapes are unchanged; time within +/-0.5%. Prediction: paired gain >= +0.1 pp on the large-seed instrument (H4.6.1). If <= -0.1 pp, coverage dominates at this budget and the line closes.

Class-balanced minibatches. With ~10-15 images per class per batch over 100 classes, a uniform permutation leaves per-class counts per batch highly variable. Stratified batches reduce gradient variance from class imbalance at zero compute, which may matter in a ~280-step run.

On E100, replace each epoch's uniform permutation with a stratified one: every batch holds floor or ceil of bs/100 images per class in random order, generated on the GPU from the trial seed inside train, so no data touches import or build. Samples, steps and shapes are unchanged; time within ±0.3%. Prediction: pooled off-seed gain on seeds 3-26 >= +0.1 pp over >=3 processes per arm. A result within ±0.05 pp closes it.

(Upward direction only) Stronger augmentation under Muon hurts: translate 4 cost ~-0.6 pp (E131), duplicated draws ~-0.9 pp (E124), and jitter hurt under SGD (E008). This refutes only the 'more augmentation' half. The weaker direction is a separate node (weaker augmentation under H12).

On E100, raise translate from 2 to 4 px (reflect padding, same fused GPU op) in the 28/32 px phases only. Time within +/-0.5%. Prediction: paired gain >= +0.1 pp on the large-seed instrument (H4.6.1). If <= -0.1 pp, the short budget is under-fitting under Muon too, and augmentation strength is closed.

Group-3 width 512 as a FLOP lever. The tile-slack premise is refuted: E117 found group-3 width cost FLOP-proportional, with 512 projected at -5.2% and 640 at +4.7%. Whether 512 loses less accuracy than the time it buys is open. The prior is low: futurebiohackers chose 576 in a ~40-config sweep because last-block width 'adds accuracy for little compute' (search), and E005 shows late capacity matters.

Free first: read the logged cuDNN/cutlass kernel names for the group-3 convs at 28/32 px (E094/E099/E106 logs). If they use 64-wide N tiles, close without runs. Otherwise run an untimed profile of group-3 widths 512/576/640 on E100 (all shapes warmed). Prediction: 512 saves >=3% of total time, and 640 adds <=1.5%. Score whichever trades better, on the large-seed paired instrument (H4.6.1). A width-512 arm must lose <=0.15 pp, beating the 0.05 pp per 1% bar.

Muon lr schedule shape. Only the floor and the warmup endpoints were tuned under Muon; the linear-decay shape was inherited from SGD. A warmup-stable-decay shape keeps a high relative step longer. Very low prior: airbench94_muon and hiverge use plain linear decay (search), WSD evidence is LM-only, E081/E083 show high-LR iterates hurt averaging, and the Muon lr level is flat (H7.1).

On E100, Muon groups only: hold the peak lr until 50% of samples, then decay linearly to the existing floor at the floor-hold point (~96%). Warmup, SGD groups and the tail are unchanged; 0-d tensors, nothing recompiles. Prediction: paired off-seed gain >= +0.15 pp on the large-seed instrument (>=100 seeds, H4.6.1) at equal time. A result within +/-0.05 pp closes schedule shape.

Effective sample size is the number of distinct (non-bit-identical) trajectories, whether they come from new seeds or new fresh processes on the same seeds. Seed pairing gives no variance reduction (E113: paired sd 0.36 = sqrt(2) x 0.26), so large-seed A/Bs are two-sample comparisons with SE = 0.26*sqrt(1/nA + 1/nB). 100 vs 100 gives SE ~0.037 pp. A pooled >=200-trajectory baseline gives ~0.032 against a 100-trajectory arm. Untimed trials (~4.5 s) make ~100 trajectories per ~8 min.

Calibrate the large-seed instrument. Untimed, through the benchmark's trial code: run E100 and a math-neutral perturbation of E100 (e.g. reordered param groups or an equivalent fusion order) on the same 100 seeds (3-102), one process each. Prediction: the per-seed sd of the paired difference is 0.3-0.5 pp, so the 100-seed paired SE is 0.03-0.05 pp, and the mean difference is within +/-2 SE of 0. Set the support/refute threshold for every later A/B at ~2x the observed SE. If the per-seed difference sd is <0.15 pp, seed pairing works and 22-seed instruments were adequate.

The off-seed side script and the scored harness differ in something that changes cuDNN or Inductor picks (shared autotune cache, memory state, launch path). That would explain why the scored 3-seed mean varies ~0.2 pp across identical-code processes (E101) while the side script's 22-seed mean varies only ~0.03 pp (E106, implying ~0.14 pp per seed).

Untimed: run E100 on seeds 0-2 through the side script in >=4 fresh processes, and compare per-seed values and the spread of the 3-seed mean with the three distinct scored E100 samples (0.7561/0.7516/0.7551). Prediction (same instrument): the side-script process sd of the 3-seed mean is 0.12-0.25 pp, and its per-seed values fall within the scored per-seed range. If the side-script sd is <0.08 pp, the side script differs from the harness and off-seed verdicts do not transfer to the gate.

Gate-instrument question. E100's 3/3 distinct scored passes (mean 0.7543) against a population off-seed mean of 0.7527, equal to E090's (~0.7525, with E090 scored at 0.7515), reflect either a persistent recipe x seed offset on the fixed seeds 0-2 or luck. If persistent, the gate must be optimized on seeds 0-2 and off-seed closes may be the wrong quantity. If luck, E100 passes the local gate only ~50-60% of the time.

Run E100 and E090 on seeds 0-2 in >=5 fresh processes each (untimed side script, or scored reruns). Prediction (persistent offset): pooled E100 seeds-0-2 mean >= 0.7538 and pooled E100 - E090 >= +0.15 pp on seeds 0-2, while their off-seed difference stays ~0. If the pooled seeds-0-2 means converge to within 0.05 pp of their off-seed means, there is no persistent offset: E100's passes were luck, and H4 must state that the gate is decided by population margin plus luck.

Decisive H8.2-vs-H11 test on the large-seed instrument. Run E108 code (2@16 + 1.75@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.5@32) against E100 on 100 seeds, paired, untimed. Prediction (H8.2): paired gain >= +0.08 pp (>= ~2 SE). If it holds, score one further step (2@16 + 2.0@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.25@32) and test whether the gain funds a ~1.5% 32 px trim. If the gain is <= -0.05 pp, H11 wins and H8.2 is refuted.

Averaging strength under Muon. Lookahead (every 3 steps at bs 1536, airbench-style ramp) and the final 8-step EMA (lerp 0.3) were never tuned under Muon. hiverge's CIFAR-10 Muon SOTA uses no training-time averaging, while airbench's lookahead uses decay 0.95^5*(t/T)^3, i.e. almost no early smoothing. Premise to verify first: removing lookahead costs >=0.1 pp on >=100 trajectories (E092 was -0.18 on 8 seeds, ~1.4 SE). If it does not, averaging strength is not a lever.

Gated on a 100-seed lookahead-removal re-measure showing >=0.1 pp loss vs the pooled E100 baseline. Then, on E100 (host-side scalars or 0-d tensors only, nothing recompiles), run arms judged on >=100 trajectories each vs the pooled baseline: lookahead ramp exponent 2 and 4 (vs the current cubic), peak decay x0.8 and x1.2, and final-EMA lerp 0.2 and 0.4 (window fixed at the last 8 steps). Prediction: at least one arm gains >=+0.08 pp (~2.5 SE vs pooled). If every arm is within +/-0.05 pp, averaging strength is closed (effects >=~0.1 pp excluded).

Late layer freezing is a real rate lever with a small, real accuracy cost. Stem + group 1 frozen from 85% of samples: -4.5% time, -0.09 pp (E118, 198 trajectories), banked (E119). From 92%: -2.5%, -0.02 pp (E120). From 80%: a further -1.7% for -0.10 pp (E133), a marginal ~0.06 pp per 1%, so 85% is at or near the optimum. Closed: group-2 freeze (E125, ~0.055 pp per 1%), FreezeOut LR anneal (E129, +0.002), and caching frozen-layer activations (search 2508.15033: fails under flip/translate augmentation). Open: BN eval mode in the frozen window (H2.20.6, FreezeOut's own design per search 1706.04983) and progressive freeze (very low prior).

Untimed first: on E100, profile per-step time and NVML energy at 32 px / bs 1024 with group 1 + stem detached vs not detached (static graph variant warmed up in build). Prediction: the detached step is >=10% cheaper, so freezing over the last 30% of samples saves >=3% of total time. Only if that holds, score the freeze from ~70% of samples and decide on the large-seed paired instrument (H4.6.1). It must lose <=0.1 pp, i.e. beat ~0.035 pp per 1%. If the profiled step saving is <6%, close without a scored run.

In the energy-bound 32 px phase, the backward of the high-resolution early layers (stem + group 1 on 31x31x128 activations: conv wgrad/dgrad, BN/GELU backward) costs >=1.3x its FLOP share of the step. Its BN/GELU backward passes over the largest activations dominate memory traffic and energy, which the fused elementwise kernels' ~30% GPU-time share (E067) and E116's ~15-20% step saving (vs ~13% backward-FLOP share) both suggest. Consequence: byte cuts at high resolution (late freeze, group-1 width, early downsampling) trade better than FLOP-equivalent cuts in group 2/3.

Untimed profile on E100 at 32 px / bs 1024 (static graphs, warmed in build): per-group backward GPU time and NVML energy, plus bytes read/written by the BN/GELU backward kernels per group. Prediction: stem + group 1 account for >=1.3x their backward-FLOP share of backward energy (>=17% vs ~13%), and the detached-variant step from E116's step-1 profile is >=15% cheaper per step. If the ratio is <1.1x, E116's saving needs another explanation (e.g. removed optimizer work for group-1 params), and N_bytes is refuted.

Group-1 width as a byte lever, never tested under Muon (H2.6 dismissed it on an SGD-era FLOP estimate). Free first: read the logged kernel tile shapes for group-1 convs. Then an untimed profile on E100 of group-1 widths 96 (1.5x64) and 112 vs 128, at 32/28 px bs 1024 and 24/16 px bs 1536 (all shapes warmed). Width 96 cuts ~13% of conv FLOPs (g1 convs plus g2 conv1 input) and 25% of the 31x31 activation bytes. Prediction: width 96 saves >=5% of projected total time, i.e. it recovers >=70% of its FLOP-proportional saving, unlike group 2's 33-60% (E080). Score only if >=5%, and judge accuracy on >=100 trajectories vs the pooled E100 baseline, requiring <=0.03 pp loss per 1% saved. Low prior: capacity is valuable on CIFAR-100 (E017, E050).

Dose-response of the stem + group-1 freeze. Measured: 92% -0.02 pp / -2.5% (E120); 85% -0.09 pp / -4.5% (E118). Remaining: 80% and 75% of samples, untimed, 100 seeds each vs the pooled E100/E116 baselines, with per-trial times from one scored row each (every freeze x renorm variant warmed; TORCH_LOGS=recompiles dev check). Prediction: 80% saves ~5.5% at <=0.18 pp; 75% saves ~6.5% at <=0.30 pp. The 85->75 marginal rate must stay <=0.05 pp per 1% for an earlier freeze to beat 32 px re-spend. If the marginal rate is >0.06, the freeze stays at 85%.

Progressive/stochastic freeze (Drop-Muon style). Over the last ~40% of samples, detach group 1 on each step with a probability rising linearly from 0 to 1. The expected frozen fraction equals the 85% hard freeze (~15% of samples), using the same two warmed graph variants selected per step on the host (group-1 params skip Muon/SGD on frozen steps; momentum untouched). Prediction: at equal total time (+/-0.5%), accuracy is >=0.04 pp better than the 85% hard freeze on >=100 trajectories each. Low prior: evidence comes only from tiny CNNs and training-accuracy metrics, and MosaicML found no Pareto gain.

Deeper late freeze: from ~92% of samples, also detach group 2's output, warmed as a third static 32 px graph variant. Measure the frozen-graph step time directly; do not project it from E122's per-group attribution, which over-predicted E116's saving by ~1.5x. Prediction: >=1.5% additional measured saving over the stem + group-1 freeze at the same point, with an extra loss <=0.06 pp on >=100 trajectories vs the pooled baseline. If the extra loss is >=0.1 pp, the late-freeze depth is capped at group 1.

Free analysis: pool E113's arms A and B (200 E100 trajectories, mean ~0.7530, SE ~0.018) as the standing baseline, and keep appending new E100 trajectories. Recompute E114 and E116 against it. Prediction: E114 ~ +0.045 pp and E116 ~ -0.09 pp (SE ~0.032 each), i.e. E116 trades ~0.025 pp per 1%. From now on every large-seed arm is compared with this pooled baseline, not a single 100-seed vector.

Acceptance rule, pre-registered and not adjusted per candidate. (1) Official safety: population mean mu >= 0.7513 on >=100 trajectories, i.e. >=3 sd of the 40-seed mean above 0.75. This is a hard policy floor; candidates that miss it by <2 SE (E133: 0.75106, ~1.3 SE short) are reported as policy rejections, not accuracy refutations. (2) Local gate: at most 3 scored attempts per code, stopping at the first row >=0.753. Every scored rerun of the same code counts toward the budget, including tip reruns attached to other experiments. E116 code already has 7 rows, which lifts the pass chance from ~61% to ~89% and voids the intended budget. (3) Every banked time is reported with Phi((mu-0.753)/0.15) and its observed pass count (E116 code: ~27% per attempt, 2/7). (4) Precondition before any final submission: submissions/arena must hold the banked E116 code, not E133's (E133 is marked feasible/improved in results.tsv and could be picked by a best-feasible-row selection). Margin policy: a cut may lower mu only down to 0.7513, and only at <=0.054 pp per 1% or funded at the 0.044 re-spend rate.

Free check on existing logs. For each same-code family with >=3 distinct scored samples and a >=100-trajectory population mean (E100: scored 0.7561/0.7516/0.7551/0.7532/0.7553/0.7534..., population 0.7530; E116: 7 rows, mean 0.7517, population 0.7521), plus the E090 family with its 22-seed mean, test whether the scored mean minus the population mean is within 2*0.15/sqrt(n) and whether the pass fraction matches Phi. Prediction: no family deviates by more than 2 SE. If E100's +0.13 pp gap (~2 SE) recurs with a consistent sign across families, add a per-recipe seeds-0-2 offset term to the gate model.

Before pairing E116's loss with an update-count gain: run E104 code (bs 1024 in all phases, +2.8% time) untimed on >=100 seeds vs the pooled E100 baseline. Prediction (H10): +0.08 to +0.15 pp (>=2.5 SE). If it lands at <=+0.04, the update-count rate is not real, and 'bs 1024 everywhere + 85% freeze' is not a net lever.

On E116 code (tip), run the 28/32 px phases at bs 1536 instead of 1024. Keep the sample-indexed schedule, rescale the SGD groups by the kilostep rule, keep Muon lr x1.25 at 32 px, keep the final-EMA window and lookahead stop pinned to the last 8 steps, and warm all freeze x renorm variants for the new shapes. Untimed, 100 seeds (3-102) vs the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. Prediction: loss <=0.05 pp (SE ~0.032) and projected/scored time -2% to -2.5%. If the loss is >=0.1 pp, the bs-1024 tail was a real purchase despite E121.

On the tip, run the 16/24 px phases at bs 2048 with the LR warmup fixed in steps, not samples (removes E043's warmup confound). SGD groups are kilostep-scaled; Muon is unchanged; all bs-2048 shapes and whiten-bias-grad variants are warmed in build. Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline. Prediction (H8 early-threshold view, E121): time about -1% and a loss <=0.03 pp. If the loss is >=0.1 pp, large early batches hurt through a channel other than update count (e.g. fewer early steps under the SGD-bias warmup).

Measure the local yardstick on E116 code. Two untimed 100-seed arms: 32 px phase -0.25 ep and +0.25 ep (sample-indexed, schedules rescaled, freeze point kept at 85% of the new total). Prediction: a symmetric slope of 0.03-0.07 pp per 1% of time, resolved to about ±0.035 pp per arm. Every later cut (depth, width, freeze, 12 px) is judged against this measured rate, both as a pure cut and as cut plus re-spent 32 px epochs.

Arm (a) 2/3/3 on the E116 base, untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled tip baseline. Outcome E127: -0.29 pp for -7.0% scored time (~0.04 pp per 1%), between the 0.25 and 0.4 pp bars. As a funded variant (re-spend ~0.29 epoch at 32 px) it nets ~-0.7%, inside error. Arm (b) 3/3/2 moves to its own node.

Only if N_depth_acc shows a hard cut costs too much: stochastic depth on group 1's (or group 3's) residual branch (conv2-conv3). Skip the branch per batch with probability p (0.3-0.5) in the 28/32 px phases, using two warmed static graph variants selected on the host; the full net is used at eval. Prediction: at equal expected time saving, accuracy loss >=0.05 pp smaller than the hard cut on 100 seeds. Low prior: the gains in 1603.09382 come from 110-layer nets with long schedules.

On the E116 base, set group-3 width to 512 (head [100, 512], Muon stacks re-batched, all freeze x renorm variants warmed). Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled tip baseline. Bar at the pure-cut rate (0.054 pp per 1%): -5.2% x 0.054 ≈ 0.28 pp. Prediction: loss <=0.18 pp. If the loss is >=0.28 pp, the cut trades no better than a 32 px trim and group-3 width closes. The tip sits on an equalized-marginal-rate frontier. Greedy banking pushed each schedule, batch, freeze and depth lever to roughly the same exchange rate, so every remaining trade of existing phases, freeze points or batch sizes costs ~0.044-0.06 pp per 1% of time (E128 0.054/0.044, E132 0.055-0.075, E125 0.055, E133 0.06, E127 0.04). Increments saturate (E121, E114). Consequence: further gains need either new zero-time accuracy (large-seed re-screens, removal ablations, weaker augmentation) or a structural change that moves the frontier. Falsifiable: a clean trim that is not a schedule-rescale artifact still costs >=0.044 pp per 1%, and a late increment buys <=0.044 pp per 1%.

The ~0.05 pp per 1% cost of phase trims reflects the marginal value of the removed training itself, not side effects of rescaling the LR/floor/renorm schedule or of shortening the whitening-bias window (the E132/E134 confounds).
